answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because sparrow only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, quartz is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any spiral approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
